cards.headline: How to stay calm with a little over a week to the written PSLE papers
bullets: Parents are sharing tips on how to help kids stay calm before the PSLE exams.
One parent lets her daughter mark her own practice papers and have family chats.
Another parent comforted her daughter after a tough Chinese oral exam.
Resources are available online to offer more advice for parents and students.

cards.headline: How to bridge the generation gap
bullets: A father reflects on how best to support his son when he graduates from university.
See the article for full details.

cards.headline: Crystal Jade closes Great World outlet, its third closure in 2026
bullets: Crystal Jade closed its Great World outlet on September 1st.
This is the third Crystal Jade outlet to close this year.
The restaurant chain is reviewing its operations and outlets.
Crystal Jade has 15 outlets left in Singapore.

cards.headline: 2 free children’s books bring Singapore’s past to life through kaya toast and ice-cream bread
bullets: Two free online children's books share stories about Hainanese food and ice-cream sellers.
One book features characters exploring Hainanese culture and food like ge bia.
The other book highlights the disappearing trade of roadside ice-cream hawkers.
These books are part of a university project to help young people share Singapore's heritage.
Physical copies will be available at some public libraries later.

cards.headline: 3 traffic cops under investigation after footage showing them riding in unsafe manner
bullets: Three traffic police officers are being investigated for riding motorcycles carelessly.
Dashcam footage showed the officers allegedly cutting off a car.
The incident happened early morning along Ubi Avenue 3.
Police say they take road safety seriously and will take action.

cards.headline: Singapore Fitness Alliance helping True Fitness, True Yoga employees find jobs
bullets: About 230 True Fitness and True Yoga staff reached out for help finding new jobs.
The Singapore Fitness Alliance is helping former True Group employees find work.
True Group cited competition and digital training as reasons for closing.
True Group has closed all 10 of its fitness centres in Singapore.

cards.headline: Virtual taekwondo makes Asian Games debut with Singapore's Darren Yap in the fight
bullets: Virtual taekwondo will debut at the Asian Games with Singapore's Darren Yap competing.
Athletes wear VR headsets and sensors to control digital avatars in virtual fights.
The sport uses technology to track movements and score virtual hits without physical contact.
Singaporean Darren Yap has trained in both traditional and virtual taekwondo for the games.

cards.headline: PM Wong warns economic frustrations can deepen social, racial divisions in Singapore
bullets: PM Wong warns economic struggles can worsen social and racial divides.
He noted online racist comments and divisions between locals and foreigners.
Wong stressed Singapore is not immune to global societal fragmentation.
He said the government will improve policies on costs and jobs.
Building trust between communities is key to national cohesion.

cards.headline: Is Singapore psychologically prepared for a terror attack?
bullets: A 14-year-old student planning a stabbing attack was arrested recently.
Psychologists say being ready for terror means acting, not just fearing.
People need to know what to do and how to report during an attack.
Learning to help others stay calm is part of being psychologically prepared.
Community efforts like psychological first aid can make crises less scary.

cards.headline: North-South Corridor construction enters its 'most challenging phase': LTA
bullets: Construction of the North-South Corridor is now in its most difficult stage.
Engineers face tough ground conditions and have to tunnel near active MRT lines.
The project involves building Singapore's longest viaduct and a deep tunnel section.
Some parts require building tunnels just a metre away from existing MRT tracks.

cards.headline: ‘Looking forward’: Tottenham Hotspur’s new faces put relegation battle behind them
bullets: New Spurs players want to focus on winning their first game, not last season's struggles.
The team has only one point from three games and has not scored yet.
New signings like Marmoush and Senesi are adapting to the coach's style.
The club narrowly avoided relegation last season and hopes for a better year.

cards.headline: UK homebuilder Berkeley urges property tax cuts as buyers stay cautious
bullets: British homebuilder Berkeley wants property taxes cut.
It suggests a 1% cap on stamp duty for first-time buyers.
Buyers are still cautious, slowing down the housing market.
Other builders also want lower stamp duty and government help.

cards.headline: Mazda 6e Fastback review: Don’t buy that Tesla Model 3 yet
bullets: The new Mazda 6e electric car costs S$235,888 with COE and is available now.
It boasts a 560 km range and can charge from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.
The car won World Car Design of the Year for its stylish looks.
Its cabin can be pre-cooled remotely and it has a useful front trunk.
The car's touchscreen system can be confusing to use.

cards.headline: San Francisco mayor declares rent emergency amid AI housing frenzy
bullets: San Francisco's mayor declared a rent emergency due to rising costs.
Rents have jumped over 25% in the last year, with a one-bedroom costing over US$4,000.
Some landlords are offering cash to get tenants to leave rent-controlled apartments.
Over 2,400 evictions have been filed this year, the highest in a decade.

cards.headline: Five decades of supporting tennis: BNP Paribas returns to back star-studded Singapore Open
bullets: Top female tennis players will compete in Singapore from Sep 21-27.
The Singapore Tennis Open has a prize pool of US$1.25 million.
BNP Paribas is sponsoring the tournament, continuing its long support for tennis.
Filipino star Alexandra Eala and last year's champion Elise Mertens are confirmed players.

cards.headline: Toa Payoh coffee shop staff caught stealing S$4,300 from stall, begs owner for forgiveness, runs away the next day
bullets: A coffee shop chef stole S$4,300 from his boss in Toa Payoh.
He admitted to stealing after his boss found money bags at his home.
The chef had previously stolen from the boss and was forgiven.
After being caught, he begged for forgiveness but fled the next day.
Police are investigating the theft.

cards.headline: Former HK actress Margaret Chung, 49, reportedly taken to ICU, thanks fans for concern
bullets: Former actress Margaret Chung was reportedly in the ICU at Chinese University Hospital.
The 49-year-old thanked fans for their concern in an Instagram statement.
She asked for privacy to focus on her health and family.
Recent photos showing her looking frail had sparked speculation about her health.

cards.headline: S'pore man, 71, threatened to blind wife, 74, with fork after she didn't give him money for lottery tickets
bullets: A 71-year-old man was jailed 12 weeks for attacking his wife with a fork.
He got angry when his wife refused to give him money for lottery tickets.
The man also threatened to blind her and hit her with a thermos and stool.
The wife suffered bruises, swelling, and a fractured nose from the attack.

cards.headline: We Took A Last Look At Punggol Container Park & Here’s What You Can Still Do Before It’s Gone For Good
bullets: Punggol Container Park closes in November 2026 for future housing.
You can still enjoy barbecue, Filipino, and Thai food there.
There's a pickleball court available for booking daily.
A CrossFit gym offers various fitness classes and drop-in sessions.

cards.headline: 16 Best Deals In Singapore This Week – 14th-20th September 2026
bullets: Get 1-for-1 teppan steaks at Bari Bari Steak's new 313@somerset outlet for 4 days.
Grab up to 80% off swimwear and accessories at the TYR Relocation Sale until Oct 31.
Students can get free Shell Select Care Packs with snacks and drinks at participating stations.
Take home up to 10 pre-loved books for free at the NLB Big Book Giveaway this weekend.
Fly to KL from $128 with Firefly Airlines, including free baggage and snacks.

cards.headline: Shell Is Giving Away Free Care Packs To P6 Students For The PSLE Season – Here’s How To Cop Yours
bullets: Shell is giving away 10,000 free care packs for P6 students during PSLE season.
Each pack has over $30 worth of snacks and goodies, including chicken essence.
P6 students can collect a pack by showing their student ID or exam slip.
The giveaway runs on September 19-20 and 26-27 at 51 Shell stations.
Parents or guardians can collect the care pack for their child.
